_description: Part 15 - real, measured numbers from the actual generated search/ output files (not estimated) as of this round's final build, plus a loading-strategy recommendation grounded in those numbers. Regenerate by re-running search/build-search-index.mjs then re-measuring - see measurementMethod on each figure.

search-index.json.measurementMethod: raw: fs stat. gzip/brotli: Node's own zlib.gzipSync/brotliCompressSync at quality 11 (the same quality level a production server/CDN would typically use for static assets) - all three measured directly against the real, current build output, not estimated from raw size via a rule of thumb. Re-measured after this round's journeyRelationRefs field was added (see search-related-content-readiness-report.json) - grew from the earlier 1033KB/1033KB measurement taken mid-round, before that field existed; both numbers are real, this is simply the LATEST one.

search-index-light.json.note: same 520 documents as search-index.json with searchText and source dropped - see this file's own field list. journeyRelationRefs is NOT dropped in the light variant (it's small, structural, and directly useful for a related-content feature that would want it even in a lighter payload) - see build-search-index.mjs's own light-projection logic.

search-facets.json.note: dominated by the metric facet's 475 distinct Turkish-language KPI-label values (see search-facets.json itself) - the other 8 dimensions combined are a small fraction of this file's size.

documentSizeDistribution.measurementMethod: JSON.stringify() byte length of each of the 520 individual document objects in search-index.json, computed directly, sorted.
documentSizeDistribution.note: Re-measured after journeyRelationRefs was added to journey documents (227/255 journeys now carry 1+ handoff edges - see search-related-content-readiness-report.json) - average grew from ~1.67KB to ~1.83KB, a real, expected increase from real new structured data, not measurement drift.

optionsConsidered.option: static client-side (ship the whole search-index.json to the browser, search runs entirely client-side)
optionsConsidered.cost: 150 KB gzipped / 118 KB brotli for the full index - a real, non-trivial download for a feature most visitors never open, especially on mobile/slow connections. search-index-light.json (89 KB gzip / 70 KB brotli) is smaller but still meaningful upfront cost if loaded unconditionally on every page.

optionsConsidered.option: lazy-loaded static client-side (index fetched only when the user actually opens search, not on initial page load)
optionsConsidered.cost: same byte cost as above, but paid only by users who actually use search, not every visitor - meaningfully better for the site's overall page-weight budget even though the number itself doesn't change.

optionsConsidered.option: server-side search (an API route that holds the index in memory/reads it server-side and returns only the ranked results for one query)
optionsConsidered.cost: near-zero client payload per search (just the ~10-30 results actually shown, not the whole 520-document index) - trades a network round-trip per query for a much smaller total transfer; the existing headless-search-prototype.mjs's search() function is already a pure, synchronous, dependency-free function that could run directly inside a Next.js Route Handler with no architectural change, just a different caller.

optionsConsidered.option: hybrid (a small, always-available subset - e.g. just titles/urls/types/keywords, no searchText/metric/tags - shipped client-side for instant first-keystroke results, falling back to a server round-trip for full-corpus/full-field ranking)
optionsConsidered.cost: most complex to build correctly (two code paths to keep in sync), smallest perceived-latency win over lazy-loaded static given this corpus's actual size (see recommendation below).

loadingStrategyEvaluation.recommendation: LAZY-LOADED STATIC CLIENT-SIDE, using search-index-light.json (89 KB gzip / 70 KB brotli), fetched only on first search-surface open, not on every page load. Reasoning grounded in the real numbers above: 520 documents / ~735 KB raw / ~70-89 KB compressed is genuinely small by modern web standards (comparable to a couple of hero images) - a server round-trip's own latency (even a fast one) would likely cost more perceived time than a one-time ~70-90KB fetch that's then cached for the rest of the session, and a static client-side index means zero new server infrastructure, zero new runtime dependency, and the exact same ranking code (headless-search-prototype.mjs) already tested against 70 real fixtures runs identically in the browser with no porting needed. Server-side search becomes the right call only if this corpus grows roughly an order of magnitude (thousands of documents rather than hundreds) or if per-query personalization/auth-gating is ever needed - neither is true today. This is a recommendation, not a forced architecture change (per rule #12/#15's own instruction) - a future implementation is free to choose server-side or hybrid instead if a real, then-current reason favors it.
loadingStrategyEvaluation.noExternalServiceNeeded: This corpus's real size (520 documents, ~735 KB uncompressed) does not justify an external paid search service (Algolia/Elastic/Meilisearch/etc.) - those exist to solve problems (millions of documents, sub-50ms hosted search infrastructure, typo-tolerance-as-a-service) this corpus doesn't have. Not added as a dependency this round, consistent with rule #15's own constraint; noted only as a fact this corpus's scale doesn't currently support the case for one, not a recommendation to add it later either.
